Each prover ran on one thread (RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1) and proved the same batch of 32,768 Falcon-512 signatures five times under samply. samply samples every thread at 250 Hz and records the CPU time each thread used since its previous sample; each stack is weighted by that CPU time, so the sampler's own pauses do not skew the split. Only stacks inside the timed prover call are kept: Aerie's prove_aggregate_measured_with_mode, and BitZ's commit_from_s2 plus prove. Each graph is scaled to the same setup's unprofiled single-thread time.

The split agrees with the harnesses' own clocks. All three provers spend at least 98.8% of their wall time on the CPU. BitZ's commit phase is 7.6% (as shipped) and 9.2% (experiment) of prove time by its own timer, and the same to within 0.1 points by samples. Span-traced runs of earlier BitZ configurations put the bridge, the sumcheck arithmetic, the ring check and the opening within one point of their sampled shares. Aerie's commit, opening and sumcheck-stage totals fall within 3% of its stage timers.

At one thread Rayon would run parallel work on its worker thread, cut off from the caller's stack. Both harnesses therefore ran the prover inside the pool (a bench-only switch), where nested parallel iterators run inline. Rayon's scheduling frames and closure-call shims are removed, so time spent in an inlined parallel closure appears in the function that started the parallel iterator. In the experiment's build the keyed-ring prover functions are marked #[inline(never)] so they keep their own frames; that is a local profiling change.

Builds: Aerie v0.2.0 as published (the cargo bench profile without LTO or a target-cpu flag, Rust 1.95). BitZ as shipped is John's falcon-poc at e140a3f3. The experiment is origin/falcon-ring-succinct at d0ed8cfc1, run with the keyed integer ring check, the one-limb bridge with 2^16 bridge rows and its small sampled prime (2^111 ≤ p < 2^112), and per-site grinding. Both BitZ builds use LTO and target-cpu=native (Rust 1.98.1), so their frames are coarser than Aerie's.

An earlier version of this page profiled the experiment with 2^13 bridge rows and the canonical ring check: 3.21 s per prove on one thread and a 1.51 MB proof. With 2^16 rows and the keyed ring the proof is 0.59 MB, but one thread now proves in 3.59 s. Two things cost the extra time: the smaller prime grinds 18–19 bits per prime-field round (0.41 s of grinding here), and the keyed ring's prover takes 0.68 s against about 0.56 s for the canonical ring. On 10 threads the other session measured 807 ms prove and 21 ms verify for this configuration.

The two timers cover slightly different work. Aerie's prove call decodes the compressed signatures, computes HashToPoint for every record and checks each signature natively before proving. BitZ's harness hands its prover decoded s2 and precomputed targets, so that work sits outside BitZ's timer. Signature decoding is marked separately; HashToPoint is inlined into Aerie's witness preparation.

Kinds of work come from frame names. A stack takes the kind of its outermost phase frame (for example integer_bridge::prove_weighted for the bridge, keyed_ring::prove for the ring check, opening::open_groups for Akita's opening). A grinding or signature-decoding frame overrides that wherever it appears. Frames under 0.3 ms per prove fold into their parent; a few system-library frames without symbols show as the library's name.
Folded stacks and plain inferno SVGs for each profile are in the falcon-flamegraph worktree under bench_results/flamegraph-20261017/out-samply.
